newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares hit new high, boosted by drugs.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares hit new high, boosted by drugs.

text.p: The Stockholm bourse ended on a new high on Tuesday after a boost from drug companies Astra and Pharmacia & Upjohn, rate-sensitive shares and Ericsson, with the U.S. expected to set the direction for Wednesday.
The bourse's general index closed up 0.97 percent at 2,146.32, a new closing high, in turnover totalling 4.6 billion crowns.

The drug sector index climbed 2.17 percent as Astra rose six crowns to 302.50 buoyed by overnight U.S. gains. Pharmacia & Upjohn gained 5.50 crowns to 244.50, rebounding from losses in the wake of last week's forecast of flat earnings in Q3.

Ericsson jumped 4.50 crowns to 177.50 after Intel Corp's stronger than expected third quarter earnings report. Market sources said Enskilda had upgraded its trading recommendations on Ericsson and Finnish rival Nokia to buys from outperforms.

A focus of morning trade was Terra Mining which resumed trading after a suspension on Monday. The company announced it was in preliminary talks over a possible merger and its shares plummeted 14.50 to 125.50 crowns.
Clothing retailer Hennes & Mauritz reversed recent strong gains, diving 50 crowns to 890 crowns.
